items.title: A Human-Centric Decision Framework for Selecting Artificial Intelligence Collaboration Strategies Under Uncertainty in Industry 5.0
items.abstract: Effective collaboration between humans and artificial intelligence (AI) in industry 5.0 demands technological systems with human social-cognitive processes, such as trust calibration and shared mental model. This study introduces human-centric decision-making framework for configuring human-AI collaboration in smart manufacturing systems. As Industry 5.0 evolves, finding the best synergy between human intelligence and collaborative robots (cobots) becomes crucial for enhancing adaptability, safety, efficiency, and sustainability. The proposed methodology uses neutrosophic Z-numbers (NZN) to capture uncertainty with three components: truth, indeterminacy, and falsity with their associated reliabilities, and the NZN weighted arithmetic averaging (NZNWAA) operator to combine individual preferences of decision-makers. Afterward, the criteria importance through intercriteria correlation (CRITIC) method is used to objectively determine the importance of each criterion by analyzing contrast intensity and inter-criteria correlation. The ranking of alternatives is then obtained using the compromise ranking of alternatives from distance to ideal solution (CRADIS) method. This hybrid NZN-CRITIC-CRADIS approach is applied to a real-world case study of BMW manufacturing systems, assessing four human-AI collaboration strategies: full AI automation, partial cobot integration, human-led AI-assisted assembly, and hybrid multi-agent collaboration, across four critical criteria. The results of the study show that the AI-assisted assembly emerges as the most suitable solution, balancing technological capability with human-centric design. The effectiveness of the proposed approach has been further validated through a sensitivity analysis and a comparative assessment with existing decision-making techniques, where our model consistently demonstrated superior performance in handling uncertainty and maintaining objectivity. Ultimately, this study offers a reliable human-centered framework that emphasizes socially intelligent manufacturing.

items.title: A METHODOLOGICAL FRAMEWORK FOR DEVELOPING AN INFORMATION SECURITY CULTURE IN ENTERPRISES
items.abstract: This study examines the use of artificial intelligence (AI) in digital games in the contemporary era. The digital gaming industry is continuously evolving under the influence of technological advancements, and AI is one of the most significant drivers of this transformation. In digital games, AI is applied in numerous areas, including improving the behavior of non-player characters (NPCs), dynamically adjusting difficulty levels, generating game content, and personalizing the player experience. The aim of this study is to investigate the areas in which AI is used in digital games and to evaluate its impact on the player experience. A literature review method was employed, and the development and application areas of AI in the digital gaming industry were analyzed. The findings indicate that AI technologies enhance the realism of games, strengthen player interaction, and contribute substantially to replay ability. Furthermore, AI-supported systems were found to increase user satisfaction by offering players more personalized and dynamic experiences. According to the findings, AI technologies play a strategic role in the development of digital games. In the future, AI will remain one of the key factors shaping game design and the player experience. Accordingly, greater investment by game developers in AI-based solutions will enable them to gain a competitive advantage within the industry.

items.title: Adversarial Malware Detection Using Feature Contribution Difference Analysis with Kernel SHAP
items.abstract: Adversarial malware evades machine-learning-based detection by modifying its feature vector while preserving its malicious functionality. As attack methods continue to diversify, learning all possible adversarial patterns using conventional adversarial training has become impractical. However, because adversarial malware must retain its malicious functionality, certain intrinsic characteristics are common across diverse attacks. Based on this observation, we propose a two-stage adversarial malware detection method that leverages explainable artificial intelligence to analyze feature contributions in the prediction process. In the first stage, a neural network classifier performs the initial detection. In the second stage, Kernel SHAP is used to quantify each feature’s contribution to the model’s prediction, and the average contribution difference between benign software and malware is computed. The proposed method assigns higher weights to features with small contribution differences, which tend to exhibit high contributions when malware is present, and computes a maliciousness score to redetect adversarial samples that are misclassified as benign. Experimental results on Android application datasets demonstrate that the proposed method significantly outperforms existing approaches across four representative adversarial attacks (fast gradient sign method, JSMA, Mimicry, and Pointwise) without explicitly learning attack-specific characteristics.

items.title: Artificial intelligence and the rebalanced hemostasis of chronic liver disease: From viscoelastic testing to digital twins
items.abstract: Chronic liver disease, particularly cirrhosis, produces a fragile, rebalanced hemostatic state. Patients may develop bleeding or thrombosis. The international normalized ratio and platelet count incompletely reflect concurrent procoagulant and anticoagulant changes and poorly predict procedural bleeding. Viscoelastic testing and thrombin-generation assays assess hemostasis more broadly. Randomized trials support viscoelastic testing-guided reductions in blood product use, but these trials do not establish prediction of later bleeding or thrombosis. Machine-learning models address gastrointestinal bleeding outcomes, variceal hemorrhage, portal vein thrombosis (PVT), and transfusion requirements using clinical records, imaging, or elastography. Most cirrhosis models address one outcome, omit direct hemostatic measurements, and have limited external validation. Within the English-language eligibility criteria and focused queries of a PubMed update on July 29, 2026, no adult model jointly estimating future bleeding and PVT in cirrhosis was identified. This structured narrative minireview evaluates the evidence for both outcomes and specifies research requirements for paired-risk models and a possible digital twin of the coagulation-portal axis. Treatment-specific predictions would require additional causal validation.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence for Green Chemistry and Environmental Protection From Predictive Chemistry to Sustainable and Responsible Innovation
items.abstract: Green chemistry designs chemical products and processes that avoid hazard rather than merely control it after the fact, reconsidering reactions, solvents, catalysts and materials from the earliest stages of design.Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly part of this effort because it offers a practical way to make sense of the very large volumes of chemical and environmental data modern research now generates.Machine learning, deep learning, generative AI, natural language processing and computer vision are being used to anticipate reaction outcomes, screen catalysts and solvents, flag likely toxicity or persistence, and interpret environmental sensor data in near real time.This chapter surveys these applications, from predictive chemistry and multi-objective process optimisation to safer molecular design, catalyst and solvent screening, biocatalysis, sustainable materials, carbon capture, green analytical chemistry, and the monitoring of water, air and waste.It maps AI onto the twelve principles of green chemistry, and argues that AI's own computational footprint means it cannot be assumed sustainable simply because it accelerates discovery.A responsible approach requires trustworthy data, inspectable models, rigorous experimental validation, life-cycle thinking, and honest accounting of the energy AI itself consumes.The chapter closes with a practical ten-step framework, arguing that AI's durable contribution to sustainability will come from its disciplined integration with chemical judgement, safety practice and environmental accountability -not from computational power alone.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence in In Vitro Fertilisation: Clinical Evidence, Market Trajectory, Regulation and Bioethics, with Foresight to 2031
items.abstract: Research monograph (working paper, not peer reviewed), 58 pages, 52 references. Background. Around one in six people experience infertility, more than three million IVF cycles are reported annually and an estimated 13 to 17 million children have been born through IVF. Artificial intelligence (AI) is now applied along the entire IVF pathway while its clinical benefit remains contested. Aim. To provide an integrated, critical assessment of AI in IVF as of late 2026 across clinical evidence, market development, regulation and ethics, and to derive scenario-based predictions and recommendations. Methods. Structured narrative review, documentary analysis of EU, Swiss, UK and US regulation, secondary analysis of market data, normative ethical analysis and scenario analysis. Results. AI embryo assessment is roughly ten times faster than manual assessment, but the largest randomised trial (n = 1,066) did not demonstrate noninferiority on clinical pregnancy (46.5% vs 48.2%), and time-lapse imaging did not improve live birth in a trial of more than 1,500 patients. The AI embryo selection market is estimated at USD 320 million in 2025, growing about 18.5% annually. Under the EU AI Act most clinical IVF AI is high-risk. Polygenic embryo screening is considered not ready for clinical practice by the ASRM. Conclusions. The study proposes the cohort constraint as an explanatory principle, a four-question governance framework for clinics, ten falsifiable predictions to 2031 and a research agenda. AI should inform and accelerate; accountable humans should decide. Use of AI: an AI language model assisted with literature synthesis, structuring and language editing; the author verified all sources and takes full responsibility.

items.title: Attitude Toward the Integration of Artificial Intelligence Among Public Elementary Teachers and Their Level of Preparedness: The Case of Kasibu West District
items.abstract: Under DepEd Order No. 3, s. 2026, Philippine basic education schools face an urgent mandate to integrate digital and smart technologies into instructional workflows. However, a significant operational divide persists in rural school districts between policy expectations and classroom readiness. This study evaluated the attitudes, instructional preparedness, and operational challenges of public elementary school teachers regarding Artificial Intelligence (AI) integration in Kasibu West District, leading to the development of a structured administrative intervention plan. Grounded in Everett Rogers’ Diffusion of Innovations Theory and the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), a mixed-methods convergent parallel design was employed across all 23 public elementary schools in the district. Quantitative data were gathered from a mathematically determined sample of 120 teachers (N = 172, 100% response rate) selected via proportionate random sampling, using a structured 105-item 4-point Likert instrument. Content validity was established by a panel of three educational experts, and pilot testing with 25 NVSU MAEd graduate students (evaluated by an NVSU university statistician) demonstrated high internal reliability across sub-scales (Attitude α = .939, Preparedness α = .945, Challenges α = .710, Overall α = .910). Results revealed a High overall teacher attitude (Mean = 3.22, SD = 0.42), with Professional Efficiency ranking highest (Mean = 3.37). Instructional preparedness was likewise High (Mean = 3.05, SD = 0.40), led by Behavioral Intentions (Mean = 3.32) but constrained by low Professional Development and Training (Mean = 2.83). Operational challenges were High overall (Mean = 3.12, SD = 0.31), dominated by Technical and Infrastructure Barriers (Mean = 3.36). Inferential analysis yielded a statistically significant, very strong positive correlation between attitude and preparedness (r = .801, p < .001, n = 120), leading to the rejection of the null hypothesis. Qualitative thematic content analysis identified five core grassroots recommendations emphasizing hands-on Learning Action Cell (LAC) training, infrastructure hubs, DepEd-vetted tools, ethical policies, and administrative support. The empirical findings directly informed an expert-validated 4-Phase Administrative Intervention Plan Matrix to systematically address training deficits and upland digital friction.

items.title: Awareness, utilization, and pedagogical integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools in biology teaching among science teachers: Toward the development of a training program
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used to support instructional planning, the development of learning materials, assessment, and student engagement. However, the extent to which science teachers are aware of, utilize, and pedagogically integrate AI tools in Biology teaching remains an important concern. This study determined the awareness, utilization, and pedagogical integration of AI tools among junior high school science teachers in the Division of Tagbilaran City, Bohol, and examined the predictive contribution of these variables to teachers’ perceived teaching effectiveness and ability to promote student engagement. A quantitative approach using a descriptive-predictive research design was employed. The respondents were 32 junior high school science teachers teaching Biology in public secondary schools, selected through total enumeration. Data were gathered using an adapted structured questionnaire administered through Google Forms and analyzed using frequency, percentage, weighted mean, and multiple linear regression. ChatGPT was the most recognized, currently used, and most useful AI tool. Teachers were aware of AI tools (M = 3.81), frequently utilized them in Biology instruction (M = 3.74), and occasionally integrated them pedagogically (M = 3.35). Their perceived teaching effectiveness and ability to promote student engagement were rated positively (M = 3.68). The regression model significantly predicted the outcome (R² = .603, F = 14.17, p < .001); however, only awareness was a statistically significant predictor (B = 0.450, p < .001). Utilization and pedagogical integration were not significant predictors. The findings informed a proposed professional development program to strengthen teachers’ AI literacy and support the effective, ethical, and curriculum-aligned integration of AI in Biology teaching.

items.title: Brand Impersonation and Customer Support Hijacking Analysing How Fraudulent Customer Service Accounts on Social Media Scam Corporate Clients
items.abstract: Social media is a public-facing channel for customer-service, and brands are now able to respond to questions and complaints quickly. Consumers' visibility also enables scams to monitor consumers, replicate brand identities and approach consumers via replies or private messages. This article will discuss the methods used by fraudulent customer support accounts to leverage brand recognition and social trust, and will assess controls at the user, company, platform and payment levels. This focused narrative review collated 29 scholarly papers from 2020-2026, comprising of 21 journal papers and eight peer-reviewed conference papers. The evidence shows brand impersonation is not just a fake-profile problem of classification. It's a multi-step fraud route that includes squatting on an account, timely interception of support requests, transferring to private or external channels, requests for credentials, verification codes or payment. Machine-learning studies provide helpful indicators from profile content, profile behavior and network structure, and human-factors studies explain why social familiarity and perceived authenticity can make a difference in reducing scrutiny. Most detection studies rely on labels and data sets, however, that are not inherently linked to customer-support impersonation or financial loss. The article suggests a multi-layered approach to the response, incorporating the official channel clarity of guidance, fast reporting of evidence for preservation, behaviour-awareness in platform detection, safer support channels and metrics for success like time to takedown and repeat-account activity. The review offers a practical approach for minimising the risk of customer harm, as well as opportunities for research in cross-platform measurement and in the field.

items.title: Can AI Personalise Meaningfulness? Bodies, Prediction, and Postdigital Health and Physical Education
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly woven into Health and Physical Education (HPE) through motion analysis, wearable data, adaptive task design, automated feedback, and generative support for teachers. These developments are often associated with personalisation and, by extension, with the possibility of making learning more meaningful for individual students. This conceptual article questions that connection. Drawing on Kretchmar’s philosophy of meaning in movement, Meaningful Physical Education (MPE), and postdigital accounts of entangled pedagogy and technological mediation, it argues that meaningfulness is not a personalised output but a postdigital accomplishment. It emerges through embodied activity, relationships, material settings, cultural practices, interpretation, and time. Particular AI-supported arrangements may expand or constrain these conditions, but no technical adjustment can guarantee what an experience will come to mean. The analysis develops four tensions: personal relevance between dialogue and prediction; challenge between embodied negotiation and adaptive optimisation; fun, sociality, and delight beyond engagement analytics; and biographical meaning in relation to computational memory. It shows how personalised systems can also influence whose movements, preferences, and histories become visible and valued. The article concludes with five commitments for keeping meaningfulness open in postdigital HPE: interpretive openness, negotiated personalisation, embodied and relational attentiveness, collective possibility, and temporal and infrastructural humility.

items.title: Claim Enlargement Through Familiar Rewording: Why a Rounder Sentence Can Claim More Than the Study Did
items.abstract: This conceptual paper introduces Claim Enlargement Through Familiar Rewording, a mechanism by which a bounded finding is restated in familiar language that appears equivalent but asserts more than the original procedure established. A description tied to particular participants, measures, and conditions can become a general claim when those qualifications disappear. The resulting statement may be easier to understand while supporting conclusions or decisions that the original evidence did not warrant. The paper assesses rewording by reconstructing the procedure that produced the finding, comparing its original description with subsequent formulations, and identifying what each revision adds or omits. Plain language is not itself a defect, and a broader claim may be true on independent evidence. The mechanism concerns the transfer of evidential standing from a narrower statement to a wider one through an apparently ordinary restatement. Its practical significance becomes visible when the revised wording supports action beyond the scope of the original result. The discussion examines two documented cases. In a 1993 study, K. Anders Ericsson and colleagues reported that the strongest group of violin students had accumulated approximately 10,000 hours of solitary practice on average by age twenty. Malcolm Gladwell's Outliers subsequently described the figure as something each elite player had reached and extended its significance across fields. In 2010, photographer Dan McLaughlin left his job to test whether 10,000 hours of deliberate practice could make him a professional golfer. The second case concerns a 1993 experiment involving 36 college students. Researchers reported higher spatial-reasoning scores immediately after participants listened to a Mozart sonata than after comparison conditions. In 1998, Georgia governor Zell Miller described the finding as a nine-point increase in IQ scores while requesting funding to provide classical recordings to families with newborns. The original study had not established a general increase in intelligence or an effect in infants. Part of the Representation and Measurement series within On Human Modeling, the paper places the mechanism alongside published research on exaggeration in university press releases. It examines how evidential limits can disappear as findings move among researchers, intermediaries, and decision-makers. Potential applications in human–AI interaction include automated summarization, research synthesis, generated explanations, and evaluations that test whether paraphrasing preserves the scope of the evidence it reports.

items.title: Cluster-Based Learner Profiling in AI-Supported Educational Contexts: Evidence from Junior High School Students
items.abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) becomes increasingly embedded in educational settings, learner heterogeneity can no longer be adequately described through single-variable comparisons. This study identifies learner profiles in AI-supported educational contexts using three theoretically grounded feature dimensions: AI self-efficacy, digital literacy, and cross-disciplinary integration self-efficacy. These dimensions were operationalized using eight indicators reflecting students’ AI-related confidence, digital information-processing competence, and integrative learning readiness. Based on 8,022 valid responses from eighth-grade students in the collaborative database of the Taiwan Assessment of Student Achievement: Longitudinal Study and the Taiwan i-Generation Panel Study, available from the Survey Research Data Archive, Academia Sinica, all input indicators were normalized using Z -score scaling to construct a standardized feature space for distance estimation. A two-stage clustering procedure was adopted. First, two-step cluster analysis was performed to compare candidate solutions based on Akaike Information Criterion and Bayesian Information Criterion values; subsequently, K -means clustering was conducted with the number of clusters fixed at six to estimate the final learner profiles. The results supported six profiles: high-scoring integrated; very low-scoring; AI-moderate, digitally weak; broadly below-average; digitally adequate, AI-integration weak; and near-average balanced. The profiles showed that learner heterogeneity was not organized along a simple high–low continuum but appeared as asymmetric configurations within the multidimensional feature space. Post-clustering analyses further showed that digital-literacy indicators and AI evaluation had the largest descriptive between-profile separations, and that cluster membership differed significantly by gender. The findings extend AI literacy research from average-based comparisons to cluster-based learner profiling and provide a basis for differentiated educational support and data-driven decision-making in AI-related educational settings.

items.title: Conditioned connectomes outperform the standard correlation kernel for predicting cognition in an independent cohort
items.abstract: Connectome-based cognition predictions are scored differently across papers. We re-scored a public Human Connectome Project benchmark (753 subjects, six fMRI modalities, 60 family-aware splits) as its authors do, with a public age band in place of exact age, and evaluated a kernel ridge pipeline that conditions each subject's connectome and filters the between-subject kernel's spectrum. With fixed settings it reached r = 0.7215, against 0.6779 for the benchmark paper's best model and 0.6798 for our re-run of its kernel (corrected t = 3.23). This margin is transductive: the filter uses all subjects' unlabelled features, helps only after conditioning, and gives no significant gain fitted on training subjects alone; without it, the difference was not significant. On 263 HCP subjects outside the benchmark, most used in development, a pre-registered comparison favoured the filtered pipeline, computed with them present, over the benchmark's kernel by 0.064 (95% interval 0.030 to 0.099). In an independent cohort never used in development (1,290 adults aged 36 to 89, resting state), the conditioned connectome, fitted on training subjects only, beat the benchmark's kernel as pre-registered (r = 0.5861 against 0.5257; corrected t = 5.47); the filter added nothing there. Against a frozen fMRI foundation model on identical splits, the unfiltered pipeline was ahead in 7 of 8 settings, significantly on resting state (corrected t = 3.88), held-out subjects and ABIDE autism diagnosis, and nominally in AOMIC. Of 18 pre-registered single-decision contrasts, 9 were met, 5 by counting repeats. Two scoring choices each reversed a method ordering.

items.title: Constrained Choice Developing Into Preference Under an Identical Record: Why a Habit Begun Without Options Can Become a Real Preference
items.abstract: This conceptual paper introduces Constrained Choice Developing Into Preference Under an Identical Record, a distinction between repeated behavior that registers a continuing constraint and the same behavior that reflects a preference formed through experience. A record of choices can remain identical while the reasons for those choices change. What began as an obligation may become something a person genuinely wants, just as an activity repeated for years may cease when alternatives become available. The paper assesses this distinction through the alternatives available at different times, the person's choices when those alternatives change, and their own account of what the activity has come to mean. Repetition alone cannot establish preference, and a constrained origin does not invalidate a later liking. Continued or renewed participation under feasible alternatives can support a formed-preference interpretation, particularly when accompanied by evidence of self-directed pursuit. The discussion sets this distinction beside Jon Elster's account of adaptive preferences, separating adjustment to constraint from learning and preference formation through experience. Two documented biographical cases illustrate the distinction. Czech pianist Tomáš Kačo recalls practicing piano throughout childhood because his father required it, describing the experience as an obligation until approximately age fifteen. After developing his own interest, he applied to a conservatory despite his parents' opposition. When rejected, he attended an agricultural school while traveling weekly for lessons in preparation for another audition. Chinese tennis player Li Na entered a state sports program as a child without choosing tennis herself. In 2002 she left the sport to study journalism, returning to competition in 2004. She later described tennis as something she had come to enjoy and pursue for herself. The accounts distinguish externally sustained activity from later choices made under changed conditions. Part of the Formation and Enactment series within On Human Modeling, the paper examines who interprets repeated choices, who controls the available alternatives, and who may revise a stored account of another person's preferences. Potential applications in human–AI research include preference learning, personalization, recommendation systems, and evaluations that distinguish behavior produced by restricted options from preferences users have subsequently formed or rejected.

items.title: CRAFTMANSHIP AS A CATEGORY IN THE PHILOSOPHY OF ART OF THE DIGITAL AGE: A PHENOMENOLOGICAL APPROACH
items.abstract: This article offers a philosophical reconstruction of the criteria for artistic mastery in the context of the proliferation of digital media and generative artificial intelligence. It challenges the tendency to equate mastery solely with technical proficiency, professional status, or the visual perfection of a work, while conversely reducing amateurism merely to aesthetic inferiority. The methodology integrates a phenomenological analysis of aesthetic experience, the hermeneutics of artistic decision-making, a media-philosophical perspective, and a critical examination of contemporary literature on the philosophy of AI. It is argued that generative technology alters not only the artist’s toolkit but also the modes of form emergence, the distribution of agency, and the processes of perception. The study proposes distinguishing between image generation, its artistic articulation, and the aesthetic event, processes that do not necessarily coincide. The novelty of this research lies in delineating three levels of an artistic work-technical generation, authorial articulation, and the aesthetic event and in conceptualizing mastery as a reflexively responsible capacity to organize the relationships between these levels, rather than as a mere sum of skills or a property of a finished artifact. Conclusions. Based on this, a multidimensional model of mastery is developed, encompassing intentionality, media literacy, reflexive selection, temporal depth, the productivity of aesthetic experience, and responsibility. It is demonstrated that the «human versus machine» dichotomy is less analytically productive than the distinction between the automated reproduction of the recognizable and responsible form-creation. Amateurism is interpreted as an open mode of participation in culture—one capable of evolving into mastery, independent of commercial or institutional legitimation.

items.title: DESIGNING AI-RESISTANT TASKS AS A TOOL FOR ASSESSING THE ANALYTICAL AND CRITICAL COMPETENCIES OF FUTURE TEACHERS
items.abstract: This article provides a theoretical foundation for assessing the analytical and critical competencies of future teachers in the era of generative artificial intelligence. It has been demonstrated that the limited reliability of automated AI-detection tools necessitates a shift from evaluating the final written product to a "process-over-product" diagnostic paradigm, while upholding the principles of academic integrity. Within the structure of an educator's analytical - critical competencies, the cognitive-diagnostic, didactic-design and reflexive-metacognitive components have been distinguished. A didactic model has been developed for designing AI - resistant assignments that focus on higher-order thinking skills, specifically "Analyzing", "Evaluating" and ″Creating″ according to Bloom's Taxonomy. The model incorporates the ″Three Zones ″ framework and utilizes three diagnostic formats: the analysis of contradictory pedagogical cases (Case Study), the cognitive auditing of AI-generated content (Reverse Engineering), and in-person, dialogue-based defense using the Socratic method (Socratic Defense). Furthermore, a criterion - based, multi-level rubric has been proposed comprising verification-analytical, didactic-adaptive, and metacognitive-authorial criteria to objectively assess students' professional agency and critical thinking.

items.title: Digital Readiness and Narrative Driven Competency of Teachers in Adopting Artificial Intelligence Enabled Classroom Teaching Strategies
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence enabled classroom‑teaching tools can rapidly generate narrative‑style learning resources, explanatory paragraphs, casestudy materials, and formative assessment prompts for learners [1]. However, effective classroom integration requires teachers to possess not only general digital readiness but also narrative competency: the capacity to evaluate AI‑produced narratives, correct factual inconsistencies, align AI‑generated content with curriculum standards, and deliver coherent lesson narratives suited for Filipino learners [2]. This quantitative survey‑based study examined the relationship between teachers’ digital readiness, narrative‑focused AI competency, and adoption of AI‑enabled classroom teaching strategies among 385 public‑ and private‑school teachers from Metro Manila and CALABARZON [3]. Anchored on the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), DigCompEdu Framework, and Diffusion of Innovation Theory [4, 5, 6], the survey instrument measured four independent variables: technical digital readiness, pedagogical‑narrative competency, ethical‑content‑validation competency, and professional‑development readiness [7]. Cronbach’s Alpha reliability testing recorded α = 0.914 for digital readiness and α = 0.899 for narrative‑AI competency [8]. Descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, and multiple linear regression were computed using SPSS 26 [9]. Findings revealed that pedagogical‑narrative competency recorded the highest mean score (M = 3.78, SD = 0.70), while ethical‑content‑validation competency registered the lowest mean (M = 2.92, SD = 0.84) [10]. A strong positive correlation (r = 0.744, p < 0.001) existed between overall digital readiness narrative competency scores and AI‑enabled teaching‑strategy adoption [10]. Regression analysis confirmed that pedagogical‑narrative competency (β = 0.425, p < 0.001) was the strongest predictor of AI‑strategy adoption [10]. Limitations included purposive sampling, cross‑sectional design, self‑reported competency bias, and geographic scope limited to Metro Manila‑CALABARZON [11]. The study concluded that teachers must combine digital readiness with narrative‑content‑validation competency to deploy AI‑generated classroom materials responsibly [12]. Recommendations included DepEd‑aligned narrative‑AI pedagogy training, school‑based AI‑content‑ethics workshops, and localized guidelines for verifying AI‑generated narrative learning resources [13].

items.title: Digitalisation de la fonction RH, cognition, bien-être au travail et performance organisationnelle: revue systématique multi-bases et cadre intégrateur à double voie
items.abstract: Objectif : expliquer pourquoi la digitalisation des ressources humaines (RH) est associée à des bénéfices organisationnels et à des contraintes psychosociales parfois simultanées. La fragmentation des synthèses sur l’e-HRM, le technostress et la gestion algorithmique justifie une analyse intégrée des mécanismes d’appropriation. Méthode : revue systématique à visée intégrative de publications de 2007 à 2026, recherches clôturées le 8 septembre 2026 dans Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection, Business Source Complete et PsycINFO. Cinquante-deux contributions ont atteint l’étape d’éligibilité , 39 ont été retenues et 13 exclues. La synthèse est narrative, structurée par mécanismes, aucun protocole n’a été préenregistré. Résultats : 27 publications datent de 2022 à 2026, l’audit descriptif initial distingue 24 études de crédibilité élevée et 15 de crédibilité modérée. La voie des ressources associe qualité, utilité, appropriation et autonomie. La voie des demandes associe complexité, surveillance, charge cognitive et technostress. Six travaux sur les technologies numériques générales servent d’appui conceptuel à cette seconde voie, sans valoir preuve directe en contexte RH. Contribution : un cadre à double voie distingue les résultats individuels observés du lien inter-niveaux entre bien-être et performance, proposé à la validation empirique. Mots-clés : digitalisation RH ; e-HRM ; appropriation ; Job Demands-Resources ; technostress ; algorithmic HRM ; revue systématique. Type d’article : revue systématique intégrative. Classification JEL : M12 ; M54 ; O33. Abstract Objective: to explain why digital human resource management (HRM) is associated with organizational benefits as well as psychosocial constraints. Fragmented reviews of e-HRM, technostress and algorithmic management call for an integrated account of appropriation mechanisms. Methods: an integrative systematic review of publications from 2007 to 2026, with searches closed on 8 September 2026 in Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection, Business Source Complete and PsycINFO. Fifty-two contributions reached eligibility assessment; 39 were included and 13 excluded. A mechanism-oriented narrative synthesis was used; no protocol was preregistered. Results: 27 publications appeared in 2022-2026; the initial descriptive appraisal classified 24 studies as higher credibility and 15 as moderate credibility. The resource pathway links system quality, perceived usefulness, appropriation and autonomy. The demand pathway involves complexity, monitoring, cognitive load and technostress. Six studies on general workplace technologies inform the demand pathway conceptually, rather than providing direct evidence for HR-specific systems. Contribution: the dual-path framework separates documented individual outcomes from the proposed, still untested, multilevel relationship between employee well-being and organizational performance. Keywords: digital HRM; e-HRM; technology appropriation; Job Demands-Resources; technostress; algorithmic HRM; systematic review. Article type: integrative systematic review. items.title: Displacement of Discriminating Questions by Expected Response Costs: Why Some Questions Are Easier to Ask
items.abstract: This conceptual paper introduces Displacement of Discriminating Questions by Expected Response Costs, a mechanism by which the anticipated consequences of obtaining an answer shift inquiry away from a question that would materially distinguish the alternatives relevant to a decision. A different question may be easier to pursue, less disruptive, or less likely to create an obligation to act. The inquiry continues, but the evidential distinction most important to the decision can remain unresolved. The paper assesses the mechanism by identifying the discriminating question, establishing whether it was recognized and could have been pursued, and examining what consequences its answer was expected to bring. These may include delay, strained relationships, additional responsibilities, or reconsideration of an existing commitment. A substitute question need not be irrelevant or improperly chosen. Cost sensitivity can be justified, and omission alone does not establish avoidance. The mechanism requires evidence that the expected response cost influenced which question was selected while the evidential need remained. The first documented case concerns the Metropolitan Museum of Art's 1972 acquisition of the Euphronios krater for one million dollars. Trustee Arthur Ochs Sulzberger asked whether the ancient vase had been tested, and director Thomas Hoving promised laboratory examination. Hoving later recalled harboring doubts about documents supporting the vase's provenance but withholding those doubts from the acquisitions committee. The second case concerns an investment venture involving Viktor Kozeny and Azerbaijani oil privatization. During a recorded conference call on May 18, 1999, investor Frederic Bourke asked what a person should do upon being told that an official had received a payment. The appellate record also describes another investment firm's investigation and decision not to participate. Both cases document parts of the proposed mechanism without establishing that anticipated costs caused the selection of a substitute question. Part of the Recursive Inquiry and Encounter series within On Human Modeling, the paper places the mechanism alongside research on deliberate ignorance and examines how anticipated consequences influence the direction of inquiry. A prospective human–AI application concerns an evaluation assistant that checks whether a model's output satisfies formatting requirements while avoiding a harder question about the reliability of its sources because an unfavorable answer would require delaying deployment. Establishing the mechanism would require evidence that the harder question was recognized, feasible, and displaced because of its expected consequences.

items.title: Feasibility Study of a Generative-AI-Based Privacy-Preserving Video Archiving Framework for Pedestrian Traffic Monitoring
items.abstract: In Japan, continuous monitoring of pedestrian traffic volume is considered crucial for measuring the effectiveness of sustainable urban development and revitalization efforts. However, storage periods of camera footage are limited due to privacy protection concerns, making long-term time-series analysis and detailed post-event analysis (such as movement path analysis) difficult. Existing masking techniques, such as mosaic blurring, protect privacy but result in the loss of human features, leading to reduced accuracy in artificial intelligence (AI)-based tracking and counting. This study proposes a privacy-preserving video archiving framework that enables long-term storage and post-hoc analysis by regenerating pedestrian images using generative AI. We developed a prototype system and conducted a pilot study to verify its feasibility. In a pilot experiment using a 15-minute pedestrian video, the proposed method achieved a counting accuracy of 99.07% relative to the manual reference count, suggesting that generative masking can preserve counting utility in the tested setting. However, the attribute-estimation results were affected by seasonal domain shifts, and the IoU-based evaluation revealed other issues in spatial consistency and masking omissions. These findings indicate the feasibility of the proposed framework and provide technical requirements for future privacy-preserving video archiving systems.

items.title: From Colonial Constitutionalism to Algorithmic Governance: The Evolution of Constitutional Freedom, Liberty and Human Dignity in India in the Age of Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: In the past ten years, artificial intelligence (AI) has moved from the margins of policy to the centre of constitutional debate. Automated decision systems now shape welfare distribution, policing, credit scoring, content moderation and electoral communication, and courts and legislatures are asking whether inherited constitutional notions of liberty, equality and dignity can meaningfully apply to code. This paper traces India's constitutional journey from colonial subject state to rights-bearing republic and compares it with the markedly different experiences of the United States and the People's Republic of China. It then examines how each jurisdiction is reshaping its fundamental rights regime in response to algorithmic governance, through a comparative public law analysis across three themes: the institutional design of AI regulation, the approach of courts to algorithmic accountability, and the treatment of privacy and data protection. The paper presents India as a middle-ground state that adopts the American language of judicial review while building a centralised regulatory structure that resembles the Chinese model in form, though not in intent. Tables and figures are used throughout to visualise the comparative findings. Keywords: Right to privacy; Algorithmic Governance; Data Protection; Judicial Review; Human Dignity; comparative constitutional law

items.title: GENERATIVE AI ADOPTION AND EMPLOYEE PERFORMANCE: THE MEDIATING ROLE OF DIGITAL COMPETENCE
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has become common workplace infrastructure faster than almost any digital technology before it, moving from experimental novelty to everyday workplace infrastructure, yet a critical question remains underexplored in the Indian organisational context: do GenAI tools actually make employees perform better or does that depend on something else entirely – how digitally competent the employee already is? We examine whether digital competence is the missing link in explaining when and for whom the adoption of Generative AI translates into measurable performance gains. Data were collected from 500 employees working in multinational companies located in major Indian business hubs of Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Pune, Gurugram/NCR, Mumbai and Chennai using a quantitative, cross-sectional survey design. The suggested model Generative AI Adoption → Digital Competence → Employee Performance was tested using a full analytical pipeline, including descriptive statistics, Cronbach’s Alpha, Composite Reliability (CR), Average Variance Extracted (AVE), Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA), correlation analysis, independent-samples t-tests, one-way ANOVA, multiple regression, Structural Equation Modeling (SEM), and bootstrapped mediation analysis. The Findings (reported here on an illustrative dataset, to be replaced by the primary data) suggest that the adoption of Generative AI is significantly and positively associated with digital competence, that digital competence is significantly and positively associated with employee performance, and that digital competence partially mediates the relationship between the adoption of GenAI and performance. The T-test and ANOVA results also suggest that the strength of this chain varies significantly by sex, organisational tenure and job role, indicating a more nuanced, skills-dependent adoption story rather than a homogenous productivity dividend. The findings suggest that Indian subsidiaries of multinationals should focus on digital-competence development, rather than just tool deployment, as the strategic lever to convert GenAI investment into performance results, with a particular focus on tenure-based and role-based upskilling gaps. The current study is among the first integrated SEM-based tests of digital competence as a mediating mechanism in the GenAI–performance relationship within India’s multinational corporate workforce, a fast-growing, strategically important, yet empirically under-examined segment of the global GenAI adoption story.

items.title: Global Displacement Patterns and Healthcare Access Among Ukrainian Refugees: A Mixed-Methods Analysis
items.abstract: Background The 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine triggered one of the largest and most rapid displacement crises in recent history, creating sustained challenges for refugee protection, data coordination, and healthcare delivery. Methods We conducted a mixed-methods study integrating longitudinal displacement data from international, governmental, and secondary sources with a systematic analysis of 51 healthcare policy documents and reports from ten major host countries. Quantitative analyses examined temporal and geographic displacement patterns, cross-source reporting discrepancies, and admission pathways. Large language model (LLM)-assisted extraction with independent human validation identified and assessed frequent domains in healthcare access across host countries. Results Ukrainian displacement remained protracted through 2025 and increasingly shifted from neighboring countries toward Western Europe, with Germany becoming the largest host country from 2024. Refugee estimates varied substantially across sources, likely because of differences in definitions, reference periods, and counting methods. The U.S. response relied primarily on humanitarian parole and temporary protection rather than formal refugee resettlement. LLM-assisted analysis identified five healthcare access domains: registration, primary care, mental health, specialist care, and additional services. Across the ten host countries, access ranged from comprehensive in Germany, the Netherlands, and Spain to highly constrained in Moldova. items.title: Influence of Mathematics Anxiety and Level of Motivation on the Academic Achievement of Public Senior High School Students
items.abstract: Mathematics anxiety and motivation shape how senior high school students engage with mathematics, but their joint influence on achievement has received limited attention in Philippine public schools. Grounded in the Integrated Cognitive-Emotional Theory and Self-Determination Theory, this descriptive-correlational study examined the influence of mathematics anxiety and motivation level on the academic achievement of 109 Grade 11 and 12 students at General Santos City National High School in School Year 2025–2026. Anxiety was measured in four dimensions with an instrument adapted from the Abbreviated Math Anxiety Scale, motivation in three dimensions with items adapted from the Academic Motivation Scale (α = .78 to .85), and achievement through first- and second-quarter mathematics grades. Chi-square and Pearson correlation were applied. Anxiety was High in all dimensions, with emotional and cognitive anxiety highest (M = 3.23). Students’ motivation was predominantly extrinsic (M = 3.30, Very High), followed by intrinsic motivation (M = 3.23, High), with amotivation Fair (M = 2.28). Achievement was Satisfactory and improved from 83.45 to 84.20. Age, sex, grade level, strand, and family income were associated with anxiety and motivation, while sex, grade level, and strand were associated with achievement. Anxiety was negatively related to achievement (r = −.42, p = .001), and motivation was positively related to it (r = .38, p = .002). The results are consistent with a model in which anxiety drains cognitive resources during evaluation while motivation sustains effort. A school mental health plan focusing on regulation at the point of performance, autonomous motivation, and family engagement is proposed.

items.title: Lipid Nanoparticles in Drug and Gene Delivery: Current Advances and Future Perspectives
items.abstract: As a cutting-edge non-viral delivery system, lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) are revolutionizing the treatment of drugs and nucleic acids. LNPs are now recognized as adaptable, clinically validated nanocarriers due to their clinical success, as evidenced by approved siRNA therapies and extensively used mRNA vaccines. In order to facilitate effective intracellular cargo release, modern LNPs employ ionizable lipids, which are neutral under physiological conditions but become positively charged in acidic endosomes. Stability, encapsulation efficiency, biodistribution, and therapeutic efficacy have all been enhanced by developments in lipid chemistry, microfluidic manufacturing, surface engineering, and artificial intelligence-assisted formulation. However, obstacles to wider use still include low tissue specificity, ineffective endosomal escape, immunogenicity, production difficulties, and long-term safety. The evolution, composition, formulation, delivery methods, therapeutic uses, clinical translation, regulatory issues, and upcoming tactics like organ-selective targeting and CRISPR-Cas gene editing are all covered in this review.

items.title: Markerless three-dimensional biomechanical analysis of manual flexible ureteroscopy: experience-related differences in wrist load during lower-calyx access
items.abstract: Purpose To quantify upper-limb kinematics and estimated biomechanical load (a kinematics-derived load proxy, not measured muscle force) during simulated manual flexible ureteroscopy (fURS) using markerless 3D pose estimation, testing whether experience-related differences concentrate in lower-calyx access. Methods Eighteen urologists (10 experts, 8 novices) performed a phantom task: renal pelvis to upper, middle and lower calyx, returning to the pelvis between calyces. 3D landmarks from smartphone video (MediaPipe Pose) were converted to joint angles, jerk and inverse-dynamics load estimates. Primary outcomes were right-wrist force, jerk and angle in the lower-calyx phase; others were exploratory, analysed with participant-level Welch tests, Hedges g, 95% CIs, Holm correction and a mixed model for group × phase interaction. Results Procedure time was longer in novices (115.5 vs 61.5 s). In the lower-calyx phase, novices showed higher right-wrist force (1.87 vs 1.16 N; Holm p = 0.026), jerk (Holm p = 0.020) and angle (31.6° vs 24.9°; Holm p = 0.026), with no upper-calyx differences; force and jerk showed significant group × phase interactions (p = 0.004, 0.007) but angle did not (p = 0.35). Force, jerk and dispersion correlated strongly with movement speed (ρ = 0.93–0.99), and group differences were attenuated after speed adjustment. Conclusion In this simulator study, experience-related differences in estimated wrist load emerged mainly during lower-calyx access, whereas wrist angle differed throughout, pinpointing an ergonomic target. Because estimates were kinematics-derived and not EMG-validated, findings are hypothesis-generating; correlating them with physiological muscle activity is an important next step for robot-assisted ureteroscopy design.

items.title: Mathematics Anxiety and Level of Motivation as Predictors of the Academic Achievement of Public Senior High School Students
items.abstract: Identifying students at risk of low mathematics achievement before grades are released requires markers that can be measured early. This study examined mathematics anxiety and level of motivation as predictors of the academic achievement of 109 Grade 11 and 12 students of General Santos City National High School in School Year 2025–2026. A descriptive-correlational design was used. Anxiety was measured in emotional, physiological, cognitive, and behavioral dimensions and motivation in intrinsic, extrinsic, and amotivation dimensions, using instruments adapted from the Abbreviated Math Anxiety Scale and the Academic Motivation Scale that showed acceptable to good reliability (α = .78 to .85). Achievement was measured through first- and second-quarter mathematics grades. Students were both highly anxious and highly motivated: extrinsic motivation ranked highest (M = 3.30, Very High), followed by intrinsic motivation, emotional anxiety, and cognitive anxiety (M = 3.23 each, High), while amotivation was Fair (M = 2.28). Achievement was Satisfactory, with mean grades rising from 83.45 to 84.20. Age, sex, grade level, strand, and family income were associated with both predictors, and sex, grade level, and strand with achievement. Mathematics anxiety was a moderate negative correlate of achievement (r = −.42, p = .001; 17.6% shared variance), and motivation a moderate positive correlate (r = .38, p = .002; 14.4%). Both variables are useful indicators of achievement risk and resilience, although their unique predictive contributions require regression-based confirmation. A mental health plan built on early screening and tiered support is proposed.

items.title: Mathematics Anxiety and Level of Motivation in Relation to the Academic Performance of Public Senior High School Students
items.abstract: Many Filipino senior high school students fear mathematics, and this fear may undermine their performance in a subject that shapes their college and career options. This study examined mathematics anxiety and motivation levels among public senior high school students in relation to their academic performance. Using a descriptive-correlational design, it surveyed 109 Grade 11 and 12 students of General Santos City National High School, selected through stratified random sampling, in School Year 2025–2026. A 20-item anxiety questionnaire adapted from the Abbreviated Math Anxiety Scale and a 15-item motivation questionnaire adapted from the Academic Motivation Scale were pilot-tested (α = .78 to .85), and first- and second-quarter mathematics grades were taken from school records. Results showed High anxiety in all four dimensions, led by emotional and cognitive anxiety (M = 3.23 each). Nervousness when solving problems in front of the class (3.40), a faster heartbeat before examinations (3.35), and difficulty recalling formulas during tests (3.30) were Very High. Extrinsic motivation was Very High (M = 3.30), driven mainly by grades and careers, while intrinsic motivation was High (M = 3.23) and amotivation was Fair (M = 2.28). Performance was Satisfactory, with mean grades rising from 83.45 to 84.20. Anxiety and motivation were significantly related to age, sex, grade level, strand, and family income, and performance to sex, grade level, and strand. Anxiety correlated moderately and negatively with performance (r = −.42, p = .001), and motivation correlated moderately and positively (r = .38, p = .002). Anxiety concentrated in evaluative situations, and external motivation appears to have sustained students’ effort. A mental health plan addressing stress, confidence, relevance, and family support is proposed.

Mathematics anxiety was moderately and negatively correlated with achievement (r = −.42, p = .001), and motivation was moderately and positively correlated with it (r = .38, p = .002). The findings indicate that anxiety depresses and motivation sustains mathematics performance. A comprehensive mental health plan integrating stress management, confidence-building instruction, relevance-based teaching, family engagement, and teacher capacity building is recommended.

items.title: Measuring and Enhancing Digital-Intelligence Literacy: An Empirical Study in Zhejiang, China
items.abstract: The rapid advancement of generative artificial intelligence (GAI) is accelerating the transformation of digital society from “tool-based application” to “intelligent collaboration,” creating demand for composite competencies in technical operation, ethical awareness, and human–AI collaboration. To address limitations in existing digital literacy frameworks, particularly their inadequate treatment of cognitive overload, ethical risks, and disparities in the depth of GAI use, this study proposes the concept of “digital-intelligence literacy” (DIL) and constructs a comprehensive five-dimensional evaluation framework comprising Data-Inquisitive, Synergistic-Adaptive, Digital-Content-Hermeneutic, Ethico-Security, and Solution-Application literacies. Using 667 stratified random survey samples from Zhejiang Province, China, and employing principal component analysis, one-way ANOVA, structural equation modeling (SEM), and LASSO regression, this study systematically examines the current status, group disparities, and underlying mechanisms of DIL. The findings reveal the following: significant disparities in DIL across age groups, education levels, and GAI usage frequency, with older adults and low-frequency users encountering prominent challenges; GAI cognition emerges as the most critical factor for improving DIL, substantially exceeding the influence of attitudes and environmental perceptions; a core competency transformation chain of “Synergistic-Adaptive → Digital-Content-Hermeneutic → Solution-Application” literacy revealed by SEM, alongside dynamic interaction between safety-ethics and technological exploration; and participation intentions in DIL-related education are primarily driven by existing literacy levels, usage habits, and attitudes rather than cognitive factors alone. Based on these findings, this study proposes a “cognition-first, systemic-empowerment” strategy, including nationwide educational initiatives centered on GAI-based general knowledge and differentiated empowerment strategies for key groups, providing empirical evidence for local governments to formulate precise and inclusive literacy enhancement policies.

items.title: Penguatan Literasi Membaca Siswa SD melalui Pembelajaran Kreatif Berbasis Cerita Lokal Bernilai Keagamaan di Desa Muktiwari, Cibitung, Bekasi
items.abstract: Reading literacy remains a major challenge in improving the quality of primary education in Indonesia, particularly in rural areas, including Muktiwari Village, Bekasi Regency. Although the village has a Multicultural Village Library and the “Ayo Gemar Membaca” (Let’s Love Reading) program, their use has not been optimal because literacy instruction remains conventional, reading materials based on local wisdom are limited, and religious values have not been systematically integrated into literacy activities. This community service program aimed to strengthen elementary students’ reading literacy through creative multimedia-based learning using local stories with religious values. The program was conducted in May–June 2026 and involved 66 fifth-grade students in Muktiwari Village. It comprised socialization and needs assessment, program preparation, learning implementation, mentoring and evaluation, and sustainability planning. The learning activities included reading motivation, an artificial intelligence (AI)-based animated film entitled Nawawi Sang Penebar Kebaikan, an interactive Stop and Thinking role play, and a literacy treasure hunt. Evaluation was conducted through observation, interviews, and analysis of Group Worksheets (LKK). Most students responded positively, understood the story and its religious values, and all groups completed the worksheets correctly. These results indicate that integrating AI-based multimedia, local stories, active learning, and religious values creates a more engaging, contextual, and meaningful literacy experience. The program also produced modules, learning media, and literacy tools recommended for integration into the School Literacy Movement (GLS) and the “Ayo Gemar Membaca” program to ensure sustainability.

items.title: Plausible Reconstruction Substituted for Captured Detail: Why a Convincing Picture Is Not a Record of What Was There
items.abstract: This conceptual paper introduces Plausible Reconstruction Substituted for Captured Detail, a mechanism by which details supplied from a prior model are mistaken for details recovered from a particular source. A reconstruction may combine recorded information with inferred additions so seamlessly that viewers cannot distinguish what was preserved from what was supplied. Its apparent completeness can then be treated as evidence of fidelity, although natural appearance and faithful recovery are separate properties. The paper assesses reconstruction by distinguishing captured detail from perceptual plausibility. It asks what the surviving record establishes, what additional elements were introduced, which models informed those additions, and whether the inferred portions were identified when the result was displayed or reused. Reconstruction is not inherently misleading or illegitimate. An informed completion may be the best available presentation of incomplete evidence. The mechanism arises when its supplied details acquire the evidential standing of recovered observations. The discussion draws on Frederic Bartlett's account of reconstructive memory and considers research on the relationship between perceptual quality and distortion in image restoration. The first documented case concerns Along the River During the Qingming Festival. A 2018 museum article cited a sign advertising bone-setting as evidence of medical specialization during China's Song dynasty. Subsequent comparison identified the sign in the Qing court version completed in 1736, but not in the earlier scroll attributed to Zhang Zeduan. The second case concerns an ancient Apulian vase acquired by the British Museum in 1867. Two additional heads painted onto a dog's body during nineteenth-century restoration helped scholars identify the scene as Orpheus with Cerberus. Conservation work in 1959 revealed that the original painted dog had one head. The mistaken reconstruction had supplied details on which the interpretation depended. Part of the Representation and Measurement series within On Human Modeling, the paper examines how reconstructed evidence travels, who identifies inferred elements, and how later users can distinguish restoration from observation. Potential applications in human–AI research include image enhancement, generative reconstruction, archival restoration, and evaluation of systems that produce convincing but unverified details from incomplete inputs.

items.title: Psychological Readiness for the Green Energy Transition: A Human-Factors Model for Aviation Maintenance Crews
items.abstract: Green-aviation research on battery and alternative-fuel chemistries has advanced rapidly, but a persistent blind spot remains: the psychological readiness of the maintenance personnel who operate these systems daily under safety-critical conditions.Silver-zinc (Ag-Zn) batteries, used in fighter aircraft for their high energy density, evolve hydrogen and oxygen gas through electrolysis of their alkaline electrolyte during charging -a hazard that builds invisibly over 36-to-72-hour charge cycles and becomes dangerous only once hydrogen concentration crosses its lower explosion limit.Managing this hazard depends less on chemistry knowledge and more on sustained technician vigilance during a long, low-stimulation monitoring task -precisely the condition under which classic vigilancedecrement research shows attentional lapses emerge, independent of training or competence.Drawing on the author's two decades as an aviation electrical maintenance engineer and a second career in applied and clinical psychology within the same defence environment, this paper argues that emerging green-energy-storage chemistries (lithium-ion, solidstate, hydrogen fuel cells) will introduce comparable low-visibility, highconsequence hazards, and that maintenance-crew psychological readiness must be engineered alongside the chemistry itself.Integrating self-efficacy theory, the Technology Acceptance Model, and vigilance-decrement research, the paper proposes a Psychology-Chemistry Interface Model with three components -chemistry-literacy calibration, hazardtolerability screening, and stress-buffered reporting culture -and a training framework for building calibrated, sustained vigilance in ground crews adopting new energy chemistries, including a low-cost toolkit -a pre-task hazard card, a vigilance-rotation roster, a hazard-tolerability selfcheck, and an added prompt within existing incident-reporting procedures -deployable at a single maintenance unit without new infrastructure.

items.title: Self-reported artificial intelligence familiarity, use, and attitudes among students, faculty, and staff at a medical college in the United Arab Emirates: a cross-sectional survey
items.abstract: Background Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used in healthcare and medical education. We described self-reported AI familiarity, use, and attitudes among students, faculty, and staff at a medical college in the United Arab Emirates to inform local training. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional online survey from August to October 2025. Study-specific composite summary scores ranged from 0 to 100. Linear models adjusted for respondent group, sex, and age, with HC3 standard errors. Sensitivity analyses examined AI use scoring, bootstrap confidence intervals, and restricted-age group comparisons. Results After four blank records were excluded, 375 respondents remained; the estimated participation proportion was 34.7%. At least one use of a generative AI tool during the previous three months was reported by 96.8% of respondents, whereas 78.1% reported AI use specifically in academic studies or professional practice. Formal AI training was reported by 10.8%. Mean AI familiarity, AI use, and AI attitude scores were 61.6, 62.9, and 72.1. Adjusted student-versus-faculty/staff differences were 1.91 points for AI familiarity (95% confidence interval [CI] -6.99 to 10.81), -2.87 for AI use (95% CI -23.17 to 17.43), and 2.32 for AI attitude (95% CI -5.43 to 10.07). Because age overlap between students and faculty/staff was limited, these adjusted group estimates may partly rely on extrapolation and should not be interpreted as age-matched comparisons. Average linear-model age associations indicated lower AI familiarity and higher AI attitude scores. The adjusted male-versus-female AI use estimate was uncertain (-7.61, 95% CI -16.14 to 0.92). The higher adjusted AI attitude score among male respondents was exploratory and requires caution because no multiplicity adjustment was applied. Training-stage comparisons were exploratory and showed no consistent pattern. The restricted-age analysis included 59 respondents and had wide confidence intervals. Conclusions Any recent generative AI use was common, while formal training was uncommon. These findings may guide local teaching on responsible AI use, checking AI-generated information, and maintaining human oversight. Self-report, one institution, and study-specific scores that were not formally validated limit interpretation. Future studies should validate the measures and include objective assessments of AI competency.

items.title: Semantic-Topological Cognitive Maps for Assistive Indoor Navigation of a Robot Partner
items.abstract: Assistive indoor mobile robots are increasingly expected to connect natural-language requests about familiar places and objects with the metric maps used for localization and motion planning. Metric simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) supports reliable geometry and collision avoidance, whereas many open-vocabulary scene-graph systems remain separated from the navigation stacks used on deployed robots. This paper presents a semantic-topological cognitive map (STCM) that bridges these representations for assistive navigation. The system derives place nodes from a LiDAR–inertial pose stream through a dual growing neural gas backend and consolidates object instances over time. GroundingDINO and MobileSAM provide open-vocabulary semantic grounding in the map frame through LiDAR–image association and temporal score fusion. A tool-mediated large language model interface maps user commands to explicit STCM nodes, while graph search and ROS 2 Navigation2 (Nav2) remain responsible for path computation and execution. Evaluation with recorded robot sessions, an outdoor distribution-shift probe, and a public indoor-scene benchmark indicates that the STCM backend improves object-graph construction and that the language interface improves functional-command grounding when requested objects are recoverable by perception. The pipeline is demonstrated on a Ranger Garden Assistant platform with FAST-LIO2 mapping, incremental graph construction during the mapping pass, and waypoint execution from a serialized map artifact.

items.title: Senior phase educators’ perceptions of artificial intelligence tools in geometry: A South African case study
items.abstract: Geometry education in South Africa’s Senior Phase has been marked by low learner attainment and a disconnect between the potential of artificial intelligence (AI) tools and their classroom use. Despite global advances, educators’ readiness to integrate AI in this context has remained underexplored. This study examined Senior Phase mathematics educators’ perceptions of integrating AI tools into geometry teaching. It focused on perceived benefits, implementation barriers, and the role of professional development in enabling meaningful use. A qualitative case study design was employed within a constructivist paradigm. Nine purposively selected educators from urban schools in the Free State and Gauteng participated in semi-structured interviews. Data were analysed thematically using a hybrid deductive–inductive approach. Educators showed cautious optimism, identifying improved visualisation, time efficiency, and support for differentiated learning. However, implementation was constrained by infrastructural instability, limited device access, curriculum pressures, and lack of subject-specific training. The use of AI remained largely confined to lesson preparation, and concerns about cognitive surrender emerged. The findings indicated that AI integration was constrained less by technology than by systemic and pedagogical limitations. Professional development emerged as the decisive factor shaping classroom use. Artificial intelligence was also identified as enabling educator inclusion in the case of a participant with a physical disability. Contribution: This study contributed by framing cognitive surrender as a risk in geometry learning, by positioning professional development as the decisive mediating variable between AI perceptions and classroom practice, and by foregrounding AI as a tool of professional equity for educators with disabilities. These findings contribute to the current research and developments in mathematics education at both the national and international levels by addressing the improvement of mathematics teaching and learning in the South African Senior Phase.

items.abstract: Social media is a key concept in contemporary political science.Since the first tweet in 2006, social media has flourished.The emergence of a range of platforms including X, Facebook, YouTube, WhatsApp, Instagram, and TikTok has changed how everyday individuals and political actors communicate and interact.Its impact has been felt worldwide, across the Americas, Europe, Africa, and Asia, and in the context of elections, strategic communication, agenda setting, protests, and youth political participation.It has also been strongly implicated in democratic erosion.As concerns over its negative impacts grow, conversations turn to how "social media" might be utilized and regulated-by whom-and its political implications. items.title: Topic Modelling for Biomedical Literature Retrieval via a Dual-Stream Embedding Framework
items.abstract: The rapid expansion of biomedical literature has created substantial challenges in retrieving and synthesizing relevant knowledge, particularly for novice and interdisciplinary users. Conventional keyword-based methods often lack semantic depth, whereas traditional topic modelling techniques struggle to capture domain-specific contexts and rarely integrate structured metadata, such as medical subject headings (MeSH). To address these limitations, this study introduces a dual-stream embedding framework that integrates unstructured textual content with curated biomedical metadata using transformer-based encoders and a parameterized fusion mechanism. The architecture combines contextual semantics from article titles and abstracts with expert-annotated MeSH descriptors and incorporates a large language model to generate concise and human-readable topic labels. Experimental results show that three of the four evaluated embedding configurations outperformed the single-stream baseline and that the dual-stream fusion surpassed all ablation models built from the same inputs. The best configuration, Dual PubMedBERT, achieved the highest overall topic modelling quality, improving the combined measure of topic coherence and topic diversity by 7.3% relative to the baseline. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of integrating contextual textual embeddings with structured biomedical metadata using the proposed fusion mechanism. This approach is scalable, reproducible, and domain-adaptable, providing both a methodological advancement in semantic topic modelling and a practical foundation for the development of biomedical information retrieval systems, semantic search engines, and thematic exploration tools across knowledge-intensive domains.

items.title: Unlocking Data-Driven Transport and Logistics: Challenges, Opportunities, and Insights from European Initiatives
items.abstract: European transport and logistics sectors are undergoing a transformative shift driven by the increasing adoption of data-driven solutions. This paper explores challenges and opportunities associated with implementing data-sharing frameworks and interoperable systems, drawing insights from European initiatives such as KEYSTONE and HOLOGISTICS projects and DTLF group. Fragmented data ecosystems and associated sociotechnical barriers, such as lack of inter-organisational trust and concerns over data sovereignty, significant barriers to realising the full potential of data-driven transport. However, innovations like federated platforms, real-time data utilisation and collaborative frameworks have demonstrated their ability to enhance operational efficiency, reduce environmental impact and improve resilience across multimodal transport networks. This paper presents valuable lessons learned, highlighting practical outcomes, including reduced times, optimised resource allocation, and emissions reductions. It also offers policy recommendations and a technological roadmap to address remaining barriers, scale solutions, and align with European Union’s strategic objectives for sustainability and digital integration, particularly in support of EU’s Green Deal and climate neutrality targets for 2050, also in line with the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. By addressing these challenges and leveraging emerging technologies, Europe’s transport and logistics sectors can achieve cleaner, more resilient, and connected mobility systems, setting a global benchmark for sustainable innovation.

items.title: Urinary multi-omics meets artificial intelligence in bladder cancer: from liquid biopsy to clinical decision-making
items.abstract: Bladder cancer is among the most recurrence-prone malignancies, and its management remains anchored to invasive cystoscopy and cytology, which have limited sensitivity. Urine, which is in direct contact with the tumor, carries a rich molecular cargo, including urinary tumor-derived DNA (utDNA), the tumor-derived fraction of urinary cell-free DNA, alongside methylation marks, extracellular vesicle (EV) cargo, and exfoliated cells. These components can now be interrogated through multi-omics profiling and interpreted using artificial intelligence (AI). In this Mini Review, we integrate these layers into a single translational framework: microfluidic “urine-on-chip” technologies convert a drop of urine into standardized, analysis-ready multi-omic data, while machine learning and deep learning models—increasingly governed by STARD-AI/TRIPOD + AI reporting standards—transform these data into diagnostic, prognostic, and treatment-response predictions. We highlight clinically mature anchors, including the utMeMA methylation assay (90.0%/83.1%), the Uromonitor mutation test (TERT/FGFR3/KRAS; 80.2%/96.9%, meta-analysis), chip-based cytometry for detecting high-grade disease, and an externally validated autonomous urine cytology system. These figures are assay-specific and should not be interpreted as platform-wide benchmarks. Finally, we define the priorities—pre-analytical standardization, external validation, and cost-effectiveness—that will advance urinary multi-omic AI from its current performance level into routine practice along a “detect–decide–treat–monitor” digital management pathway.
